event.canonical_title: Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash at Miami International Airport
event.summary: An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport after overrunning the runway, resulting in five fatalities and five injuries. The incident occurred when the plane, arriving from Puerto Rico, struck several vehicles on the ground. Investigations by the FAA and NTSB are underway to determine the cause of the crash.

timeline.title: Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash in Miami Under Investigation
timeline.summary: An Amazon cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport, resulting in a crash that killed five people and injured five others. The aircraft struck two vehicles on the ground, including a cleaning crew van and an SUV. Investigators have recovered the flight data and cockpit voice recorders as the FAA and NTSB begin their investigation into the incident.

event_overview.title: About Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash at Miami International Airport
event_overview.subject: Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash at Miami International Airport
event_overview.summary: On September 6, 2026, a Boeing 767 cargo flight operated by 21 Air for Amazon overran a runway after arriving at Miami International Airport from San Juan, Puerto Rico. The aircraft struck ground vehicles and caught fire; five people were killed, and the crash is the subject of a federal safety investigation whose cause had not been determined as of September 8.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The accident occurred at about 2 p.m. local time on September 6, 2026, at Miami International Airport in Miami, Florida.

facts.label: Flight and aircraft
facts.value: FAA identified the flight as 21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft that had departed Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

facts.label: Casualties
facts.value: Five people were killed after the runway overrun struck ground vehicles; authorities also reported injuries. Reporting on September 8 said those killed were occupants of a van used by plane cleaners.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating. Its process gathers evidence before issuing a final report that determines probable cause, so early facts should not be treated as conclusions about why the crash occurred.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the initial fatal crash and the next-day investigation developments, not the full recovery, airport-operations impacts, victim identifications, or the eventual NTSB findings.
